messages:
marta (eng-runtime): Heads-up, we just got a customer report: structured JSON payloads are missing keys and sometimes contain bogus fields after the morning rollout.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-18_09:12:31 -> fused-kernel-selector-v2 promoted to prod (canary 5%).
raj (eng-ml): I saw a similar eval delta on the regression dashboard: +4.7% token-level KL on the JSON schema tests after selector switch.
lee (eng-platform): Any correlation with batching changes? I changed the batch_threshold from 24->16 for latency SLOs in the same rollout.
marta (eng-runtime): Yes — selector picks the new fused_fp8_int4_v2 kernel when seq_len <= 32 and batch_size >= 2. The reduced batch_threshold means more requests hit that path.
sam (eng-sre): Customer stacktrace/log excerpt attached: "parse_error: expected \"fields\" but got \"user_meta\"" — looks like structural mismatch rather than pure hallucination.
raj (eng-ml): Uploading a quick profile snippet from canary:
```
[trace] chosen_kernel=fused_fp8_int4_v2 seq_len=28 batch_size=2 residual_scale=0.0625
[quant] calib_scale=0.083 -> runtime_scale=0.078 (per-layer 4)
[perf] tokens/sec=1420 p50=28ms
```
marta (eng-runtime): The residual_scale value is suspicious — the fused kernel applies a different post-rescale fudge than the previous kernel (we inferred a factor-of-1.25 on some layers). That can perturb logits and break deterministic structured decoders.
lee (eng-platform): Can we force the selector to prefer the stable_fp8_v1 kernel for the affected model family while we triage?
marta (eng-runtime): Yes, we can set kernel_override=model:stabledoc->stable_fp8_v1 in routing. Patching now to the canary.
perf-bot: canary patch applied to 5% traffic for model stabledoc.
raj (eng-ml): Running targeted evals with our JSON schema suite (1000 prompts) on both kernels. Initial run: stable_fp8_v1 error rate=0.8%, fused_fp8_int4_v2 error rate=5.1%.
sam (eng-sre): Rolling the selector change back or pinning is fine, but we should also track why the fused kernel is altering residual scaling. Any recent kernel code changes?
marta (eng-runtime): There was an optimization: merged residual_add + requant_op into a single fused path to save memory copies. It looks like scale accumulation order changed (req vs clamp). I'm adding a unit test for exact-rescale invariants.
lee (eng-platform): I've bumped the batch_threshold back to 24 for the pool to reduce exposure. Need a postmortem if this regresses any latency SLOs.
raj (eng-ml): Sharing differential logits example (token probs for field name):
```
stable_fp8_v1: "fields": 0.87, "user_meta": 0.03
fused_fp8_int4_v2: "fields": 0.12, "user_meta": 0.71
```
marta (eng-runtime): That is exactly the pattern — scale drift moves mass away from expected keys into low-prob noise tokens -> parser picks wrong key.
sam (eng-sre): Action items?
marta (eng-runtime): 1) Keep pinned kernel to stable_fp8_v1 for affected model family (lee done). 2) Revert fused residual fusion until we add rescale-invariant unit tests (assigned to me). 3) Run a focused quantization calibration pass on a held-out prompt corpus to see if new calib reduces delta (raj). 4) Add a perf regression dashboard comparing token-KL across kernel variants (perf-bot / eng-runtime).
raj (eng-ml): I'll run calib passes and post eval artifacts here. If calib fixes <0.5% delta we can consider reintroducing, otherwise revert fusion.
perf-bot: created ticket INF-5286: "kernel-residual-fusion: validate rescale invariants + perf/eval comparison".
marta (eng-runtime): Forensics note: the issue only surfaced when both reduced batch_threshold AND selector change coincided. Individually neither would have caused widespread user impact.
lee (eng-platform): Agreed — this is a classic interaction between batching heuristics and kernel selection. I'll add a gating rule: don't change batch_threshold and selector in the same rollout window.
sam (eng-sre): Marking customer incident Sev-2 for now. I'll coordinate comms with support.
marta (eng-runtime): I'll follow up with a minimal reproducer and a small unit test that asserts exact-match on a canonical JSON decode prompt across kernels. ETA end of day.
raj (eng-ml): FYI, while fused gave ~12% tokens/sec improvement in microbenchmarks, quality hit is unacceptable for structured outputs. We'll capture cost/quality tradeoffs in the ticket.
lee (eng-platform): Thanks. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
